title: The Choir of the Glass Steppe Anew
premise: Freya Nystrom, a beast-speaker who has spent years hiding her gift behind the ledgers of the Meridian Guild, is forced into the open when a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom—a tongue that beasts understand and that awakens the sleeping wards of the Glass Steppe. As the Guild's masters hunt the child and Freya's own gift marks her as a traitor to both human and beastkind, she must choose between loyalty to the people who sheltered her and the truth that her silence helped bury an ancient war. Across thirteen turns of the moon, Freya carries the child toward the Steppe's heart, losing allies, memory itself, and finally her invisibility. In the end she speaks the old language aloud before warring hosts, trading her hidden life—and part of her memories—for a fragile peace sealed in glass.
about_author: Xanthe Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct trade languages before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse at the edge of a salt flat, where they claim the wind occasionally answers back.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Introduces the Meridian Guild's warehouse of traded wonders and Freya's careful double life: meticulous bookkeeper by day, secret beast-speaker by night. When a cart-horse whispers a warning about 'the thirteenth moon,' she dismisses it—establishing her habit of not listening. Emotional beat: the comfort and quiet cost of invisibility.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A child arrives at the guild door during a salt storm, barefoot, unafraid of the cold, speaking syllables no scribe can transcribe. The child grips Freya's wrist and the words resolve—not into meaning, but into feeling Freya's gift translates. Emotional beat: dread blooming under wonder; Freya realizes the beasts outside have gone silent, listening.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya secretly questions the warehouse vermin and learns fragments: the child's language was last spoken before the Glass War, when beasts and humans broke their covenant. She falsifies the intake ledger to hide the child—her first deliberate act of treachery against the Guild. Emotional beat: guilt braided with fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Oskar Vey's POV. Vey notices the ledger discrepancy but responds with unsettling generosity, assigning the child to Freya's care. He reveals he knows about 'gifted' employees and offers protection—for a price to be named later. Emotional beat: warmth laced with trap; the reader sees what Freya cannot.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. An old beast-speaker's rhyme surfaces in the archives: when the thirteenth moon completes, the Steppe's wards fail unless someone speaks the covenant renewed. Freya calculates the deadline—weeks away. The child, whom she names Ash, begins teaching her words through dreams. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking; hope and terror arrive together.

chapters.title: Salt and Smoke
chapters.summary: Ash's POV (rendered as fragmented, sensory perception). Ash experiences the guild through smell and sound, recognizing Freya as 'the one who hears.' A Guild auditor arrives hunting unregistered gifts; Ash hides among the beasts, who shield the child without being asked. Emotional beat: trust forming between species where none should exist.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Question
chapters.summary: Auditor Sela Brann's POV. Sela interviews the staff, sharp and fair, and senses Freya's evasion. She isn't the enemy Freya expects—she lost family in the border raids and wants the truth about why the beasts have stopped attacking caravans. Emotional beat: an adversary who might become an ally complicates Freya's paranoia.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Vey names his price: the child, delivered to the Steppe's edge where 'buyers' await—remnant factions of the old war who will pay a fortune for a living relic. Freya pretends to agree while planning escape. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing; loyalty to the Guild dies quietly over tea.

chapters.title: Flight Across the White
chapters.summary: Freya and Ash flee at night with Sela unwittingly covering their trail. The steppe is beautiful and lethal; Freya bargains with migrating elk for passage, spending her gift openly for the first time in years. Emotional beat: exhilaration of a hidden self finally used—but each use leaves her weaker, forgetting small things.

chapters.title: What Was My Mother's Face
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya discovers the true cost of her gift: every act of deep speech erodes her own memories. She can no longer recall her mother's face. Ash comforts her in the old language, which now lives in Freya's dreams. Emotional beat: grief; the theme of memory made flesh—the price of survival is selfhood.

chapters.title: The Herd That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Sela catches up to them but instead of arresting them, reveals what she found in Guild records: Vey has sold steppe secrets for years, prolonging the border wars for profit. She joins them. Emotional beat: alliance forged in shared anger; loyalty redefined around truth rather than institution.

chapters.title: Wardstone Village
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The trio reaches a village built atop a dormant wardstone whose guardian—a stone-bound ancient beast—recognizes Ash's language and tests Freya. It shows her visions of the original covenant and its breaking. Emotional beat: awe and shame; history indicts both sides, not just humans.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Glass
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Vey's hired hunters close in; a running battle across mirrored salt flats scatters the group. Ash is taken. Freya, concussed, loses a whole year of memories. Emotional beat: despair and disorientation—the midpoint catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Tent
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash is caged among relics in Vey's buyer camp and discovers the 'buyers' are descendants of the war's exiles, desperate, not evil—they believe the child can restore their stolen homeland. Ash begins to speak to them. Emotional beat: empathy across enmity; even captors are survivors paying their own price.

chapters.title: Trading in Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya and Sela infiltrate the camp using Freya's ledger knowledge—she knows exactly how the Guild prices miracles. They negotiate Ash's release by offering the location of the mother wardstone. Emotional beat: Freya weaponizes her old life; the bookkeeper becomes the trickster.

chapters.title: Vey's Confession
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Vey's POV. Confronted, Vey justifies himself: he watched the first war devour his family and believes controlling the covenant's renewal is the only way to prevent another. He releases Ash—not from mercy, but because he wants Freya to reach the wardstone and fail publicly. Emotional beat: a villain who is also a survivor; the theme of loyalty vs. truth embodied.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Moon Wanes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. One turn remains. The group races to the Steppe's heart, guided by beasts gathering from every horizon—an army of animals walking peacefully beside human exiles. Freya has forgotten Ash's arrival day, her own surname, half her life. Emotional beat: solemn determination; she memorizes what matters onto paper like a ledger.

chapters.title: The Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. At the heart of the Steppe, the wardstone plain hums. Human armies and beast hosts face each other across the glass, both believing the other will break the covenant. Ash stands between them and begins the old language—but falters; a child alone cannot renew what adults broke. Emotional beat: terrible stillness before the climax.

chapters.title: Freya Speaks
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax. Freya steps forward and gives the covenant her voice, pouring her remaining memories into the old tongue—her childhood, her mother, her name. The wards blaze; the thirteenth moon completes mid-sentence. She finishes speaking as a person with almost no past, witnessed by both armies. Emotional beat: sacrifice at full price; truth spoken at last.

chapters.title: After the Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. The armies stand down, unbound by the renewed covenant's terms: shared stewardship of the Steppe. Vey surrenders his ledgers to Sela's new archive rather than face war-crime trials. Ash refuses to be a relic and chooses to stay with Freya. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won relief; justice without vengeance.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya relearns herself through the ledger she wrote before sacrificing her memories—reading her own handwriting like a stranger's letters. Some pages are missing; some losses are permanent. But when a horse greets her by name, the gift remains, gentler now. Emotional beat: mourning and tenderness; identity rebuilt from choice rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, now fluent in both tongues. A year later, the Steppe hosts a school where humans and beasts teach each other language. Freya, the guild's former bookkeeper, keeps a new kind of ledger: a record of everything the covenant must never forget. On the wind, the steppe sings. Emotional beat: resolution as ongoing work—peace kept, not won.
